frontier.hypothesis: F29 (carried, still the only live technical avenue if the function is ever un-parked) — because sched1's in-block priorities are flat and its class tie-break is inert on all measured chassis, sched1's output is a deterministic function of (pre-sched RTL order, dependence edges, latency queue); therefore the set of pre-sched LUID orders that replay to target's 14-insn sequence is COMPUTABLE, and the search collapses from 'which C spelling' to 'which LUID order, and can C emit it'.
frontier.mechanism: schedule_block picks ready[0] (sched.c:3966) and prepends (3970-3975); rank_for_schedule (2398-2456) resolves flat priorities by INSN_LUID; insns enter the ready list via schedule_insn's queue_insn latency path. A replay needs only the LOG_LINKS already printed in system.i.sched plus MIPS load latency 2 — on disk for four chassis in tmp/grind/saEft01Init/s16/.

A universal negative is proof-grade for the whole argument-block axis; a hit names the exact C to write. Do NOT start with another argument-spelling sweep (67 forms banked) or another permuter campaign (measured dead twice, on two objectives).
